key_insight: For this VQE benchmark, direct Riemannian optimization on each gate did not outperform a well-tuned unconstrained Euler-angle Adam baseline in practice.
engineering_relevance: For quantum algorithm engineering, the result suggests that adding manifold-optimization machinery to per-gate VQE training may not deliver real gains unless the benchmark and optimizer details are validated carefully.
method: Optimize each single-qubit gate directly on U(2) with Riemannian methods
Compare against Adam on an Euler-angle parameterization of the same unitary, using matched initial unitaries and tuned learning rates
Test metric, retraction, and momentum transport variants to check whether the conclusion changes
evidence_signal: On a validated hydrogen-chain benchmark, the two methods were interleaved in final error and success rate, with no measurable practical advantage for the Riemannian approach.
watch_item: Beware of false positives from flawed baselines or retractions, especially non-unitary Cayley-style updates, boundary-optimal learning-rate grids, and benchmarks that are too trivial.
paper_title: A Controlled Null Result for Per-Gate Riemannian Optimization in VQE
